title: New Jersey AG Launches Civil Rights Investigation into Delaney Hall After Three Detainee Deaths
excerpt: New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced a civil rights investigation into Delaney Hall, the GEO Group-operated ICE facility in Newark, after multiple detainee deaths and reports that ICE and GEO had blocked state health inspectors from entering the facility.
content:
On August 7, 2026, New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced her office's Civil Rights Division was opening a formal investigation into Delaney Hall, a privately operated ICE detention facility in Newark run by GEO Group Inc.

  • The investigation was triggered by at least three deaths connected to Delaney Hall — including the death of Edwin Lopez-Cornejo on August 1 — as well as documented reports of contaminated food, extreme temperatures, overcrowding, and at least one active tuberculosis case.
  • Governor Mikie Sherrill stated that ICE and GEO Group had blocked the state's efforts to conduct health inspections at the facility, calling the refusal to allow oversight "totally unacceptable."
  • The attorney general issued investigative subpoenas to GEO Group and ICE, focusing on whether employees violated the civil rights of people detained there.
  • ICE's rule eliminating required reporting of post-release deaths — eliminated in June 2026 — was cited as contributing to underreporting of the full death toll at the facility, as at least one death occurred shortly after a detainee was "discretionarily released" during a medical emergency.

Sen. Cory Booker called for closure of Delaney Hall, saying "a body count is not normal," but was rebuffed by Senate Republicans. Congressional members wrote to DHS Secretary Mullin citing the three deaths as "a red, flashing warning light that ICE continues to ignore."
source: Philadelphia Inquirer / ABC7 NY / FOX 5 NY
